+# External product and browser-cloud workspace (gh-2364)
+
+This is the host contract for branded Fa workspaces and provider-neutral drive
+and JSONL-session synchronization. The harness ships **no live cloud provider,
+host account, backend URL, or credential**. A host supplies each capability.
+
+## Stock compatibility
+
+`FaProductConfig.stock` has no endpoints or cloud feature flags. Existing hosts
+keep the `Fa` title, stock build, `fah_web_fs` IndexedDB database and
+`flutter-app` service-worker cache. `product_config.js` ships with null values;
+a branded build replaces it. `faNetwork` is not inherited by a branded profile:
+it requires both an explicit feature flag and product-owned endpoints.
+
+## Profile and static web build
+
+A profile is external JSON, not a source-tree edit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "productId": "host-product",
+  "displayName": "Host Workspace",
+  "description": "Host-owned workspace",
+  "storageSchemaVersion": 1,
+  "themePackId": "host-theme",
+  "themePack": {
+    "name": "Host Theme",
+    "version": "1.0.0",
+    "colors": {"dark": {"accent": "#2E7D32"}}
+  },
+  "driveAliases": ["/health"],
+  "authEndpoint": "https://auth.host.example/authorize",
+  "apiEndpoint": "https://api.host.example/v1",
+  "driveEndpoint": "https://drive.host.example/v1",
+  "sessionEndpoint": "https://sessions.host.example/v1",
+  "oauthCallback": "https://app.host.example/oauth/callback",
+  "legalLinks": {"privacy": "https://legal.host.example/privacy"},
+  "featureFlags": ["cloudSync"],
+  "brandAssets": {
+    "icon192": "icon-192.png",
+    "icon512": "icon-512.png",
+    "favicon": "favicon.png",
+    "splash": "splash.png"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Build from any host checkout:
+
+```sh
+dart run scripts/build_product_web.dart \
+  --profile /path/to/product.json \
+  --assets /path/to/assets \
+  --output /path/to/output-web
+```
+
+`--validate-only` validates without building. Icons must be square PNGs at
+192/512 px; `maskable192`/`maskable512` are optional and fall back to the normal
+icons. Favicon and splash are required. Absolute/parent/backslash paths,
+credential-shaped fields (including nested metadata), non-HTTPS endpoints
+(except loopback development), malformed metadata and invalid assets fail
+BEFORE Flutter runs. Output is staged and atomically renamed only after HTML,
+manifest, splash, `product_config.{js,json}`, icons and service-worker
+namespaces all succeed.
+
+OAuth accepts only the exact configured callback and expected non-empty state.
+Storage keys use `fa-product:<id>:schema:<n>`, with a SHA-256 tenant+subject
+account partition. Upgrading `storageSchemaVersion` creates a new cache; the
+service worker deletes only caches under the same product root, never stock or
+another product. No profile becomes executable trusted markup.
+
+## Identity and account switching
+
+`CloudIdentity` contains the verified immutable tenant/subject, device id and
+monotonically increasing `authGeneration`; email is not accepted as a subject.
+`ProductStorageCoordinator` swaps namespaces and `web/fs_store.js` closes FS,
+drive and cloud-session handles. Old operations fail their generation fence and
+cannot write into the newly active account.
+
+## Drive
+
+Hosts construct `DriveSyncEngine` with their `RemoteDriveProvider`,
+`DriveSyncStore`, `ExecutionEnv`, `DriveMountScope` and `CloudIdentity`.
+`IdbDriveSyncStore` is the browser CAS implementation; Memory stores support
+deterministic tests. Stock never constructs the engine.
+
+Only `/drive` and explicitly declared aliases are accepted. Unicode NFC and
+case-collision keys, POSIX traversal checks and sensitive path exclusions are
+in `DrivePath`; `.dap`, logs, saved keys, wallets and OAuth secrets are not
+syncable. Provider quotas, cursors and idempotency keys are isolated by
+provider/connection/tenant/subject/mount.
+
+Uploads carry bytes, SHA-256, conditional base revision, auth generation and a
+stable operation id. The durable outbox survives offline/restart, flushes FIFO,
+replays after a post-remote/pre-CAS crash, and rejects key/payload substitution.
+Precondition failures become an explicit conflict; only Keep local or Use
+remote resolution permits a write. `DriveSyncController` exposes localOnly,
+syncing, synced, conflict, planInactive, quotaExceeded,
+providerReauthRequired and permanentError to Files/Recent surfaces. Stock Files
+has no cloud row or action.
+
+## Cloud JSONL sessions
+
+`CloudSessionRepo` decorates the existing `SessionRepo`; local create/open/fork/
+append/delete complete first. `CloudSessionStorage` queues the latest JSONL
+after local writes. `CloudSessionSynchronizer` uploads complete record-id
+batches with conditional revisions and idempotency keys. Revision races merge
+record ids instead of comparing mtimes. Pull materializes parents before forks,
+rewrites parent paths to local paths, and moves the active pointer with an
+explicit sync marker. A bounded remote read failure retains local bytes and the
+pending outbox. `IdbCloudSessionSyncStore` supplies browser persistence/CAS.
+
+Local `delete()` is deliberately local-only. `closeRemoteBranch()` is the
+separate explicit remote tombstone operation. `CloudSessionShareLink` accepts
+only allowlisted HTTPS hosts, a stable session id, expiry, positive maxReads and
+read-only capabilities; account/cache credentials and write grants are invalid.
+
+## External-provider readiness
+
+`CloudProviderReadiness` classifies `stub`, `mvp` (including full-scan fallback
+when delta cursors are absent) and `complete`. `CloudProviderErrorMapper` maps
+401/402/403/409/412/413/429/5xx and validates revision/hash/delta payloads.
+`StubRemoteDriveProvider` performs no network and returns `featureDenied`.
+
+External authors run `runRemoteDriveProviderContract` against an isolated test
+account/root. It checks conditional create, same-operation replay,
+key/payload-substitution rejection, stale-base conflict, download hashes and
+conditional delete. The function requires `allowMutations: true` to prevent
+accidental production traffic.

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.

- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.

  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,

user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts

host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;

🚨 **BLOCKING: remote tombstone for a locally-missing file crashes `DriveSyncEngine.pull` and permanently stalls drive sync**

`_pullRemoteDelete` (drive_sync_engine.dart:29) calls `env.remove(path.absolute)` **without** `force: true` — per the `ExecutionEnv.remove` contract, a missing path is an error without `force` — and `pull()` runs `_pullRemoteItem` in an unguarded loop *before* the CAS save, so one tombstone aborts the entire pull and nothing (including the cursor) is persisted.

Reproduced against the real engine (`MemoryDriveSyncStore` + `MemoryExecutionEnv`, provider feed containing `deleted: true` for `/drive/notes/never-here.txt`):

```
PULL THREW: FileError(notFound, /drive/notes/never-here.txt): No such file or directory
```

Real-world trigger: another device creates and deletes a file between this device's pulls (or a first pull whose delta feed contains historical tombstones). Every subsequent pull replays the same tombstone, fails at the same point, and never advances state — drive sync is stuck for that mount until manual intervention.

Fix: `env.remove(path.absolute, force: true)` here (and consider the same at line 111 in `enqueueDelete` for the double-delete case), plus a regression test that pulls a tombstone for a path never materialized locally.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `themePack` string values bypass the markup filter and land as live `</script>` markup in the branded `product_config.js`**

The themePack validation (fa_product_config.dart:193) checks only shapes and *keys* (`name`/`version` are `String`, `colors` is a `Map`, no `wallpaper`/`code`/`script`/… keys) — the **values** are never passed through the `_text` filter that correctly rejects `<`/`>` for `displayName`/`description`. `_publicProfile` then embeds the raw themePack via `jsonEncode` into `product_config.js`, which `index.html` loads as a classic `<script src>` — and Dart's `jsonEncode` does not escape `/`, so any `</script>` inside a value terminates the script element early and the rest executes as markup. This contradicts the invariant this PR itself documents at `docs/product-cloud.md:70`: "No profile becomes executable trusted markup."

Reproduced through the real code path (`FaProductConfig.fromJson` → `stageBrandedShell`), profile accepted, emitted file:

```js
window.__faProductProfile = {"productId":"host-product",...,"themePack":{"name":"x","version":"1.0.0","colors":{"dark":{"accent":"</script><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>"}}},...};
```

The same hole exists via `themePack.name` (its slug must merely equal `themePackId`, which any slug-shaped id satisfies). Text fields are already protected, so this is an inconsistent boundary in exactly the validator the P0 milestone advertises. Profiles are programmatically generated for hosts, so a benign template value ("Tom & Jerry <default>") breaks the shell silently, and a hostile profile gets script execution in the branded app origin.

Fix (either or both): validate every themePack string value with the same `_text` rules as `displayName`, or escape the script context on emission (`jsonEncode(...).replaceAll('</', '<\\/')` for `product_config.js`). Add a rejection test mirroring the existing `_valid(displayName: '<script>…')` case.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the cloud-session sync cursor is dead state — never consulted and never advanced**

Two compounding defects make the persisted `cursor` field non-functional:

1. Line 198 starts listing from the local `null`, never from the persisted `snapshot.cursor` — compare the sibling `DriveSyncEngine.pull`, which passes `cursor: snapshot.cursor`.
2. The final save (line 231) passes the loop-exit `cursor`, which is **always null** (the `do/while` only exits when `cursor == null`), and `CloudSessionSnapshot.copyWith` uses `??` semantics so `copyWith(cursor: null)` keeps the old value. The stored cursor is therefore never written with a real value either.

Consequence: every pull re-lists the *entire* remote session set (all pages) and relies on `_alreadyMaterialized` to skip downloads — correctness holds, but the delta-pagination contract of `RemoteSessionProvider.list(scope, cursor)` is never used and the cost grows with the remote session count. There is no test asserting cursor persistence (the only `cursor` mention in `cloud_session_sync_test.dart` is a fake-provider parameter).

Fix: seed the listing from `snapshot.cursor`, advance it per page (persisting `nextCursor` even when a later page fails, if partial progress should survive restarts), and give `copyWith` a way to store an explicit null (sentinel or a `setCursor` parameter). Add a test: pull page 1 of 2 → snapshot.cursor == page-1 cursor; second pull resumes instead of full-scanning.

import json, subprocess, re

# 1. JSON validity + contract shape
with open('outputs/pr_review.json') as f:
    review = json.load(f)
assert review['recommendation'] in ('APPROVE', 'REQUEST_CHANGES', 'BLOCK')
assert review['generalComment'] == 'outputs/pr_review_general.md'
required = {'path', 'line', 'startLine', 'side', 'comment', 'severity'}
for c in review['inlineComments']:
    assert required <= set(c), c
    assert c['comment'].startswith('outputs/pr_review_comments/'), c
    assert c['severity'] in ('BLOCKING', 'IMPORTANT', 'SUGGESTION', 'NIT'), c

# 2. census consistency with inlineComments
sev = [c['severity'] for c in review['inlineComments']]
assert review['issueCounts']['blocking'] == sev.count('BLOCKING') == 2
assert review['issueCounts']['important'] == sev.count('IMPORTANT') == 1
assert review['issueCounts']['suggestions'] == sev.count('SUGGESTION') == 0
assert review['issueCounts']['nits'] == sev.count('NIT') == 0
# verdict mapping: blocking >=1 -> REQUEST_CHANGES (not BLOCK: no data loss / hosted-secret exposure)
assert review['recommendation'] == 'REQUEST_CHANGES' and review['issueCounts']['blocking'] >= 1

# 3. every inline line exists as an ADDED line in the PR diff (new files: RHS line == file line)
for c in review['inlineComments']:
    target = subprocess.run(['sed', '-n', f"{c['line']}p", c['path']], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    assert target, f"empty line {c['path']}:{c['line']}"
    diff = subprocess.run(['git', '--no-pager', 'diff', 'origin/main...HEAD', '--', c['path']],
                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    assert f'"{target}"' not in target  # sanity
    added = [l[1:] for l in diff.splitlines() if l.startswith('+') and not l.startswith('+++')]
    assert target in added, f"{c['path']}:{c['line']} not an added diff line: {target}"
    # new file -> RHS numbering == file numbering; verify hunk header covers the line
    hunk = re.search(r'@@ -0,0 \+1,(\d+) @@', diff)
    assert hunk and int(hunk.group(1)) >= c['line'], c['path']
print('JSON contract: OK')

# 4. comment files exist with severity markers
import os
for c in review['inlineComments']:
    assert os.path.isfile(c['comment']), c['comment']
    body = open(c['comment']).read()
    marker = {'BLOCKING': 'BLOCKING', 'IMPORTANT': 'IMPORTANT'}[c['severity']]
    assert marker in body.split('\n')[0], (c['comment'], body.split('\n')[0])
print('comment files: OK')

# 5. general comment: sections + size
lines = open('outputs/pr_review_general.md').read().splitlines()
text = '\n'.join(lines)
assert 'Summary' in text and 'Key Issues' in text and 'Next Steps' in text
assert len(lines) <= 22, len(lines)
assert text.count('path:') >= 5  # ranked digest lines present
print(f'general comment: OK ({len(lines)} lines)')

# 6. no stray forbidden outputs
assert not os.path.exists('outputs/response.md')
assert not os.path.exists('outputs/pr_review_general-2.md')
print('no stray outputs: OK')
EOF

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Two blocking defects verified on the real code paths: a remote tombstone for a locally-missing file crashes `DriveSyncEngine.pull` (drive sync stalls permanently), and `themePack` values bypass the markup filter, emitting live `</script>` into the branded `product_config.js` against the invariant documented in `docs/product-cloud.md:70`. One important issue: the cloud-session sync cursor is dead state (never consulted, never advanced), so every pull full-scans the remote set. Verified green: root cloud/product/build suite 102/102, focused Flutter boot/product/Files tests 29/29, `dart analyze` clean on all changed files.

**Key Issues**:
1. 🚨 `lib/src/cloud/drive_sync_engine.dart:299` — unforced `env.remove` on pull-delete crashes the whole pull (PoC: `FileError(notFound)`).
2. 🚨 `lib/src/product/fa_product_config.dart:193` — themePack string values reach `product_config.js` unescaped (PoC: profile accepted, `</script><script>alert(…)</script>` emitted).
3. ⚠️ `lib/src/cloud/cloud_session_synchronizer.dart:198` — persisted `cursor` never passed to `provider.list`, always overwritten with null.

**Ranked digest** (real but not thread-worthy):
- `lib/src/cloud/drive_sync_store.dart:106` — `copyWith` uses `??`, so `providerDetails`/`retryAt`/`remoteSha256` can never be cleared; a synced file keeps its stale error text.
- `lib/src/cloud/cloud_session_repo.dart:114` — every append re-reads, re-hashes, base64-encodes and JSON-clones the whole JSONL → O(n²) on long active sessions.
